title: Pattern search methods for user-provided points
contribution: A pattern-search algorithm in which a user routine (e.g. physics-based geometric moves in molecular geometry) proposes trial points that are projected onto the mesh by a cheap integer program and also used to order the poll, with serial and MPI Fortran 95 codes.
problem_entry: Expensive unconstrained problems in molecular geometry, where the user can propose energy-lowering points by physically relevant transformations; how to use them without losing pattern-search convergence (p. 1).
key_idea: Evaluate f only at the mesh point nearest the user point (integer program (1)); in the poll, choose the positive basis best aligned with the user direction and poll in increasing-angle order (pp. 1-3).
assumptions: None stated in the note; convergence is deferred to TR [1] (the S025 paper); W = {n e_i} keeps the projection at O(|V|n) flops (pp. 1-3).
proof_devices: none (no theorem; convergence deferred to [1], p. 1)
experiments: none; software description only (Fortran 95, MPI, two user routines with effort parameters, p. 4).
positioning: Builds on Torczon, Lewis–Torczon and Audet–Dennis pattern-search theory; cites Meza–Martinez and Hart for direct search and evolutionary methods in molecular problems (pp. 2, 4).
writing: Four-page announcement: motivation in one paragraph, pattern-search primer, full algorithm box, software paragraph; no theorem or numerics (pp. 1-4).
limits_future: No limits or future work stated; theory and numerics live in the companion report [1] (S025) (pp. 1, 4).

title: Local convergence of a primal-dual method for degenerate nonlinear programming
contribution: A stabilized primal–dual interior-point method (componentwise floors in the Newton matrix plus acceptance of infeasible unit steps with superlinear residual decrease) that converges q-quadratically under MFCQ instead of LICQ, without a centrality condition.
problem_entry: Local interior-point theory assumes LICQ, which fails generically for optimal control with state bounds when n_y >> n_u; follow Wright's stabilized SQP to work under MFCQ (p. 2).
key_idea: Two changes to classical primal–dual: floors of the order of the distance to S on X and Z in the Newton matrix (replacing centrality), and acceptance of a unit step that leaves the orthant when negative parts and the residual drop superlinearly (pp. 3-6).
assumptions: C^2, KKT, strict complementarity, second-order sufficiency for all multipliers, MFCQ; iterates assumed to enter a strictly complementary neighbourhood (pp. 3-4, 7).
proof_devices: error bound: residual ||(grad l, g, min(x,z))|| = Theta(dist to S) under MFCQ + SOSC (3.9) (p. 5)
SVD of the active-constraint Jacobian and orthogonal change of variables (Lemma 4.1 part A, pp. 7-8)
Theta(residual) block M22 shown nonsingular by contradiction with full column rank of grad g (part B, pp. 9-10)
step O(residual) (Lemma 4.1) + unit step gives residual O(residual^2) (Lemma 4.2) + induction + Cauchy-sequence single limit (Theorem 4.3, pp. 7, 12-14)
positioning: Extends Wright's stabilized SQP to primal–dual methods; contrasts with Ralph–Wright and Tseng, who need centrality and monotonicity; lists LICQ-based interior-point theories including Vicente's own (pp. 2-3).
writing: Two modifications announced in one paragraph (p. 3); the long proof is split into labelled parts (A)-(E) with headings (p. 7); a Discussion section states the main assumption's weakness (p. 14).
limits_future: Neighbourhood-entry assumption is significant; strict complementarity failure not covered; proposes index-set guessing or Wright's LP-based identification to start from any nearby point (pp. 3, 14-15).

method_links.note: Primal–dual Newton skeleton kept; only the coefficient matrix and the step-acceptance rule change (acceptance widened to infeasible unit steps); local and derivative-based.

title: Local analysis of a new multipliers method
contribution: A new augmented-Lagrangian multipliers method for optimal-control-structured NLP that updates the bound multipliers of the states explicitly (nonnegative without projection) and the state-equation multipliers implicitly, with partial-exactness theorems, local linear/superlinear convergence and a dual interpretation.
problem_entry: Optimal control/design with state bounds (c_y nonsingular); classical multipliers methods must impose nonnegativity of inequality multipliers explicitly; make the bound multipliers the explicit ones (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Eliminate state-equation multipliers via the adjoint formula, put them into a Fletcher-type augmented Lagrangian, minimize within bounds, and read the new bound-multiplier update from the subproblem's first-order conditions (pp. 2-3, 8).
assumptions: f, c C^3 with c_y nonsingular; LICQ, second-order sufficiency and strict complementarity at the solution (pp. 3, 8).
proof_devices: two-way exactness bridge: first- and second-order conditions transfer between penalized and original problem for small penalty (Theorems 4.2-4.4, pp. 6-7)

experiments: none (numerics announced for a forthcoming paper, p. 16)

title: Space mapping: Models, sensitivities, and trust-regions methods
contribution: Organizes the mathematics of space mapping: sensitivities of the map for vector-valued models, globally convergent trust-region methods for space-mapping surrogates (including an inexact blended surrogate), and a regularity theorem showing that a scalar-model surrogate is regular but can be flat and kinked.
problem_entry: Space mapping (Bandler et al.) grew up in engineering design; the paper sets out to organize its mathematical and algorithmic aspects: sensitivities of the map, provably convergent TR methods for its surrogates, and the surrogate's shape (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Differentiate the argmin that defines the map to get sensitivities and an adjoint-type surrogate gradient; compose linear models with the quadratic merit so Powell's Cauchy bound and standard TR theory apply; define the scalar map by closest matching point (pp. 3-6, 10).
assumptions: Quadratic merit H; unique argmin; G(x) invertible; P well defined and smooth (flagged as strongest and problem dependent); scalar case: P point-to-point, admitted strong (pp. 2-3, 6-7, 14).
proof_devices: sensitivity equation G(x) J_P(x) = J_c(P(x))^T J_f(x) from differentiating the optimality condition (pp. 3-4)
Powell's Cauchy bound for the composed quadratic model, then Conn–Gould–Toint global theorem (pp. 5-6)
Carter-type relative gradient error condition (17) for inexact sensitivities (pp. 8-9)
weight w_k -> 0 transfers surrogate stationarity to the fine model (Corollary 2.1, p. 9)
three-part case analysis (coincide / flat / kink) for regularity of g_P (Theorem 3.1, pp. 11-12)
positioning: Builds on Bandler et al., Bakr et al. (Broyden, TR globalization) and Conn–Gould–Toint theory; reorganizes rather than criticizes; notes the Bakr et al. choice of using c directly may not satisfy the Cauchy condition (pp. 1-2, 4-5).
writing: Two parallel parts each ending with a discussion-and-extensions subsection (pp. 10, 13-14); assumptions frankly graded (strongest, problem dependent) (p. 7); worked 1-D example introduced before the theorem to guide the proof (p. 11).
limits_future: Strong well-definedness assumptions; point-to-set map and nonsmoothness when m <= n; flat surrogates mean abandon SM when flatness appears; extensions to second order, line search, quasi-Newton, Hilbert spaces, Dennis–Li–Tapia nonsmooth TR (pp. 7, 10, 13-14).

title: Numerical behavior of a stabilized SQP method for degenerate NLP problems
contribution: A Matlab study of Wright's stabilized SQP with constraint identification (sSQPa) on twelve degenerate NLP problems and on feasibility problems, showing fast local convergence and convergence from remote points without globalization, and documenting failures.
problem_entry: sSQPa has a superlinear local theory for problems without LICQ or strict complementarity but no documented numerics; target: NLP subproblems in global optimization (pp. 1, 5).
key_idea: Restate sSQPa for mixed constraints and test it with practical adaptations (least-squares initial multipliers, tuned decrease parameter), several starting points and feasibility-mode residual measures (pp. 3-9, 15-18).
assumptions: C^2 with Lipschitz second derivatives, MFCQ, KKT, second-order sufficiency; no LICQ, no strict complementarity (p. 2).
proof_devices: none new; theory restated from Wright [12] (Theorem 1, Lemmas 1-3, pp. 5-7)
experiments: Matlab, no globalization, 12 degenerate problems x 3 starting points, log-error/residual vs iteration plots, iteration comparisons with NPSOL/SNOPT/NITRO/LOQO on two problems plus a restated Anitescu table, ID0 identification table, 57-trial feasibility comparison of four measures and two infeasible problems (pp. 8-18).
positioning: Presented as a numerical companion to Wright's sSQPa theory [12]; compares against established NLP solvers and restates Anitescu's comparison (pp. 3, 9, 13).
writing: Problem-by-problem narrative with one sentence of verdict each; failures and their structural reasons reported (pp. 9-15); no conclusion section (p. 18).
limits_future: Failures on HS13, problem 10 and ID0 misidentification reported; no globalization; global-optimization use stated as ongoing work (pp. 1, 10, 13, 15).

key_idea: lambda(x,w) = least-squares multiplier; P(x,w,mu) augmented Lagrangian; minimize within bounds and set w_{k+1} = grad P, nonnegative by the subproblem's KKT conditions (pp. 2-4).
assumptions: f, h C^3, grad h full rank; nondegeneracy, second-order sufficiency, strict complementarity (pp. 3, 6).

title: Space mapping for optimal control of partial differential equations
contribution: A Tikhonov-regularized (smooth) space mapping, a new Broyden update that adds a secant condition from the surrogate gradient, and a trust-region aggressive space-mapping algorithm for PDE optimal control, tested against nonlinear multigrid on two semilinear elliptic problems.
problem_entry: Discretized PDE control is large and nonlinear; MG/OPT needs convexification and uses only grid coarsening; space mapping can use simpler surrogates, but S062's definition creates kinks (pp. 1-5).
key_idea: Define P by penalized least-squares matching (smooth when G(x) is nonsingular), update its Jacobian by a Broyden formula with a relaxed second secant condition damped by sigma_k, and globalize by trust regions (pp. 3-9, 12-13).
assumptions: g, g-hat, r, r-hat C^1 (C^2 for smoothness), P single-valued, G(x) uniformly nonsingular; TR theorem needs Carter's condition on B_k, not shown for Broyden matrices (pp. 4, 7).
proof_devices: marginal-function regularity (Rockafellar) for directional derivatives of g_P (Theorem 2.1, p. 4)
Carter's relative-error condition imported for TR global convergence (Theorem 4.1, p. 7)
closed-form least-squares solution of the two-secant problem via vectorization and one Lagrange multiplier (Proposition 5.1, pp. 8-9)
sizing relation alpha*lambda(x) ~ g-hat(x-hat) - g(x) between smooth and nonsmooth definitions (p. 5)
experiments: Two 2-D semilinear elliptic control problems; CPU-ratio vs FAS nonlinear multigrid (0.089-1.040) and res-ratio vs prolongated coarse solution (0.011-0.044) over coarsening levels; new vs classical Broyden ablation (0.072 vs 0.089); sigma_k sensitivity (pp. 16-22).
positioning: Repairs Vicente's own S062 nonsmooth mapping; builds on Bandler et al. and Bakr et al.; contrasts with Lewis–Nash MG/OPT (flexibility, nonconvex globalization) (pp. 2-5).
writing: Early and repeated disclaimer that SM is not a fast fine-grid solver (pp. 3, 19); theory imported with an explicit statement that investigating it further is not the authors' goal (p. 7); conclusions list concrete untreated cases (p. 22).
limits_future: Not a fast fine solver; CPU advantage vanishes at fine coarse levels; control bounds not treated; fine-gradient approximations untested; future: several coarse models, level-specific optimizers, SM-based fast solver (pp. 3, 15, 19, 22-23).
